_comment: The painted map's colours. Resource packs can replace this file; F3+T reloads it. Every value is optional: one left out or unreadable keeps the built-in value. Distances are in blocks. Since MM-8 the land is painted in each block's real colour: the average of its top texture (from the resource packs) times its biome tint.
_colour: the pull toward a muted painted palette, and the brush. saturation: scale of each colour's saturation (0-2); value: how far each colour's brightness is pulled toward a mid tone (0-1); brush_size: how many blocks across the brush's windows are (0-16; 2 or less: no brush). The brush settles mixed ground into soft patches of one colour while borders between colours stay sharp.
_classes: optional overrides: classes 0-7 are grass, forest floor, sand, rock, snow, dirt/mud, ice, lava. A class given a 'colour' is painted in it instead of its blocks' real colours, tinted by the biome's grass or foliage colour as much as its 'tint' says (0 none, 1 fully). None is set by default, e.g. "classes": { "3": { "colour": "#9c978d", "tint": 0 } }
_water: deep_at: depth at which water is fully deep; deep_dist: distance from the shore at which it is; shore: the pale band along the shore, shore_width blocks wide; tint: how much the water's own colour (its biome's) tints it, 0-1
_edges: softness: how soft the border between two colours is (0.01 sharp, 1 a wide blend); warp: how far, in blocks, borders and coasts wander from the data
_forest: darken: how much full canopy darkens the leaves' colour; stipple: strength of the soft brush texture over forests
_contours: only drawn when contours are switched on in the map (off by default); interval in blocks of height
_finish: grain: paper grain over the whole map; vignette: how much the corners of the fullscreen map darken
_fog: the fog over unexplored land: colour (paper a shade darker by default), edge: how far, in blocks, the explored land fades into it (8-256), clouds: how strong the static cloud texture in it is, and how much it roughens the edge (0-1)
